note: The field verification of the frame-scheduler fix (201/4-01), taken 2026-08-30 minutes after the defect was found. A timer defect that no test can see needs a capture: `schedule(true)` stored the idle timeout's handle and nothing dropped it when the timer FIRED, so `wake()` read a dead handle as a pending idle wake and armed a second `requestAnimationFrame` on top of the one the drawn frame had already armed — two entries into the loop for one displayed frame, the second 0-2 ms behind the first. The signature is frames faster than a vsync interval, which nothing else in this loop produces. BEFORE (app e3c4831): 192 of 808 frames under 8 ms, 23.8 %. AFTER (app 6bdffcf, the same circuit and the same `?overlay=0`): 6 of 229, 2.6 % — a 9x drop, and the six that remain are the legitimate case (a real touch waking a genuinely idling loop). THE COMPARISON IS THE RATE, NOT THE DISTRIBUTION: the two windows read different paks (12-08 against 28-08, because the panel's out field changed between them) and are different lengths, so the moving-frame figures beside them are context rather than an A/B — mean 30.6 -> 27.5 ms, p50 24 both, p95 80 -> 56. What the fix is claimed for is the wasted loop entries and the wake-ups they cost, which on this device is battery; it is claimed for no frame-time improvement. Device MGA-LX3 / ARM Bifrost, 360x320 CSS at DPR 2, no timestamp-query.
